question.text: Let $A(-3,2)$ and $B(-2,1)$ be the vertices of a triangle $\mathrm{ABC}$. If the centroid of this triangle lies on the line $3 x+4 y+2=0$, then the vertex $C$ lies on the line :

solution.text:
Let $\mathrm{C}=\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ $$ \mathrm{A}(-3,2) $$
Centroid, $\mathrm{E}=\left(\frac{x_1-5}{3}, \frac{y_1+3}{3}\right)$ Since centroid lies on the line $$ \begin{aligned} & 3 x+4 y+2=0 \\ \therefore \quad & 3\left(\frac{x_1-5}{3}\right)+4\left(\frac{y_1+3}{3}\right)+2=0 \end{aligned} $$ $$ \Rightarrow \quad 3 x_1+4 y_1+3=0 $$ Hence vertex $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ lies on the line $$ 3 x+4 y+3=0 $$
